newsitem.title: JAPAN: Matsushita steps ahead of Sony in Europe TV battle.
newsitem.headline: Matsushita steps ahead of Sony in Europe TV battle.

text.p: Matsushita Electric Industrial Co moved a step ahead of rival Sony Corp in their battle to enter European digital TV markets with a tie-up with British Sky Broadcasting Corp, analysts said on Wednesday.

"Matsushita has been trying to grasp the initiative in the European digital TV market and its huge set-top box market," said Katsuhiko Sugiyama, president of research company Musashi Business Development Co.
"One point up for Matsushita," Sugiyama said.
Sony, with its strong connections to Hughes Electronics Corp of the United States, has already sold millions of set-top boxes to American DirecTV satellite broadcasters.
The two firms are also in head-to-head competition over studio-use digital broadcasting equipment, as TV stations around the world are rapidly switching to digital equipment.
This market had been dominated by Sony, but Matsushita is seen to be rapidly catching up, particularly with its latest version of the DVC Pro digital transmission equipment.

Matsushita said on Wednesday that it would form a joint venture worth 265 million pounds with BskyB, British Telecommunications Plc and Midland Bank to deliver digital interactive services in Britain.
Matsushita is to take a 15 percent stake in the venture, while BSkyB and BT each take a 32.5 percent and Midland Bank the remaining 20 percent.
The venture, British Interactive Broadcasting Ltd (BIB), will enable high street businesses to offer interactive services, including home shopping and banking, to television viewers.
BSkyB said on Wednesday that the new company had divided its order for a total of one million set-top boxes between Matsushita and three other manufacturers.
BIB's set-top boxes will allow viewers to enjoy an initial 200 channels of BSkyB's digital satellite programming when connected to an ordinary TV.
They will also be designed to be capable of upgrades to receive either digital terrestrial or cable signals, Matsushita said.
Britain plans to start digital terrestrial broadcasting in the first half of 1998.
BIB expects its interactive services to be available from the summer of 1998, following the launch of BSkyB's digital broadcast service next spring.
Analysts expect sales of the set-top boxes to start contributing to Matsushita's profits next business year.
"Sales prospects are good because the set-top boxes can also be used for digital terrestrial broadcasting," said Nanako Sakaguchi, an analyst at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson.
BSkyB said it had placed orders for one million set-top boxes as part of its drive into digital television.
Matsushita said it expected sales of 12 million digital television set-top boxes over 10 years.
Some analysts said those estimates were too conservative.
